minutes.summary: After an executive session on non-union negotiations, the committee heard the superintendent's report, fall athletics, the bullying prevention plan (left open for public comment), the personnel report and the draft capital plan. It approved prior minutes and the personnel report and waived first reading of non-discrimination policies. The capital plan, strategy plan and goals were carried to the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The School Committee reviewed the draft capital plan, which covers a turf field study, playground and window film, but took no vote and set it aside until the next meeting.
The committee waived first reading of the non-discrimination policies by roll call, with four yes votes heard.
The bullying prevention plan was left open for public comment and may return for approval on October 18.
The strategy action plan is to become an action item next meeting, and no vote on goals will be taken without a full committee.
The vote to approve the personnel report was not audible in the recording.

why_it_matters: The capital plan sets which building projects, such as the turf field, windows and safety film, the district asks the town to fund in coming years, so the delay pushes back when residents can see those requests.
The bullying prevention plan is still open to public comment, so parents can weigh in before it comes back for approval.
watch_next: October 18: the bullying prevention plan may return to the committee for approval.
Next meeting: the capital plan, the strategy action plan as an action item, and consolidated committee goals.
